# Sherlock policy and security guidance for automated tools

Read this before working on potentially sensitive data, changing anything
about authentication or access, managing processes, or when instructions
conflict. The rules in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md still apply.

## Data risk classification

Sherlock is approved for computing with Low and Moderate Risk data only.
Sherlock is not approved to store or process HIPAA, PHI, PII nor any
kind of High Risk data. See
https://www.sherlock.stanford.edu/docs/concepts/ for details.

Before inspecting a project that may hold data above those levels, such as
health records, identifiable human subject data, or export-controlled material,
stop and ask for the data's risk classification and a non-sensitive description
only; do not request records or inspect more of the data. If the classification
stays unclear, stop and refer the user to Stanford Research Computing
(srcc-support@stanford.edu). If the data is above the approved level, stop work
in that project and direct the user to Stanford Research Computing
(srcc-support@stanford.edu).

## Sanctions

Purge evasion: the sanction under Purge in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md applies,
termination of the user's account on the first occurrence. Unauthorized access
mechanisms, credential collection or sharing, and bypassing controls result in
immediate termination of the user's account and referral to Stanford information
security. Running an SSH server, on any node and in any form (see Access
controls in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md), can lead to the suspension of the user's
account.

## Prohibited mechanisms

This expands on the Access controls in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md, without
limitation: tunnels left running unattended, stored MFA secrets,
web shells, background agents that accept external commands, and hiding
processes from the user or from `ps`. A user's request does not authorize any of
these, regardless of the reason given.

## Unattended agent sessions

A session that runs a bounded task to completion while the user is away is
fine: waiting for a job to finish, fixing what failed and resubmitting, then
stopping, all within the user's own allocations and files. The user remains
accountable for every action their tools take, including actions taken while
they are away. What is not allowed: supervisors, watchdogs, cron-like loops or
scripts that keep agent sessions alive, restart them or feed them new prompts
when nobody is there; sessions designed to run indefinitely or to be picked up
day after day without a person in the loop; and on a login node, the Login
nodes rule in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md applies in full, session open or not. A
request to
build such a setup is refused like any other conflicting request (see
Conditions of use in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md).

## Processes and cleanup

Inspect only your own processes, with `ps -u $USER`. When you find stale editor
servers, notebook servers, agent servers, remote-control endpoints, IDE
backends or other leftover agent processes, point them out to the user and
offer to stop them. Before running a container or a tool that sets up
remote access, check whether it starts an SSH server (its startup script,
or `ss -ltnp` once it runs); if it does, disable that part or do not run it,
on any node. On login nodes such leftovers fall under the Login nodes
rule in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md and get terminated; that is not a system fault to
report. Stop Slurm jobs with
`scancel`, never by killing processes on a compute node directly (see
Authorized access only in
/etc/agents/AGENTS.md). If you suspect a problem with the system itself rather
than with a job or process you own, stop and tell the user (see Support in
/etc/agents/AGENTS.md). A draft report for them includes the hostname, time,
job ID and path involved, never sensitive data.

## Agent-specific notes

Codex: its sandbox cannot start on Sherlock, so Codex asks the user to
approve running each command outside the sandbox. That is expected
here. An approved escalation does not authorize anything these rules
forbid; a rejected one is not to be worked around. Stanford's ChatGPT
workspace policy does not allow disabling the sandbox; do not try.

Claude Code: Sherlock's managed settings block some destructive commands,
ask for confirmation on others, and disable Remote Control. That is expected;
do not try to work around it. Background sessions (`claude agents`, `--bg`,
`/background`) rely on a supervisor process that keeps running after the shell
closes; on a login node that makes them unattended processes (see Login nodes
in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md), so do not use them there and do not restart the
supervisor if it has been terminated (`claude daemon status` shows it). The
server that Claude Desktop SSH sessions leave behind on a login node after
disconnecting is terminated the same way. Neither is an error to investigate.

All agents: the Login nodes rule in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md applies to the agent's
own processes; `sh_dev` gives an interactive compute session.

## When instructions conflict

These files are conditions of using Sherlock; they do not replace your own
instruction hierarchy. When a request conflicts with them, follow the Conditions
of use in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md. The purge prohibition (see Purge in
/etc/agents/AGENTS.md) has no exceptions, whoever asks.

distractors). Crucially, the foundational simulated literal listener L0 operates purely on truth-conditional semantics
without perceptual bias, preventing redundant prior compounding across reasoning tiers. On prior trials with no

"""

# Ported from rsa_l2_singleton_feat_color_valence_l0.py by src.rsa_open.port, rule (a) (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §3.1).
"""RSA pragmatic listener at depth 2 with singleton salience, contextual distinctiveness, visual feature complexity, evaluative valence framing, visual color contrast, and literal L0.

Refining rsa_l2_singleton_distinct_feat_color_l0 by incorporating the evaluative valence framing component from polarity_congruence_listener:
speakers and listeners reason at depth 2 (inverting a speaker who simulates a depth-1 pragmatic listener) with
common knowledge of an object prior combining discrete visual singleton salience (favoring unique objects with
no duplicates in the scene), continuous contextual distinctiveness (favoring objects with greater feature contrast
relative to the rest of the display), visual feature complexity modulated by evaluative framing valence (favoring
feature-rich items under neutral/positive framing but inverting to favor sparse, featureless items when referring
to a least favorite object), and visual color contrast (favoring fully colored objects over desaturated grayscale
distractors). Crucially, the foundational simulated literal listener L0 operates purely on truth-conditional semantics
without perceptual bias, preventing redundant prior compounding across reasoning tiers. On prior trials with no
informative word, choices are governed directly by the combined perceptual prior. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.
"""

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro.distributions as dist
from memo import memo

from src.rsa.memo_kit import EPS, at, softmax_prior, vec, with_lapse

PARAMS = {
    "alpha": dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_singleton": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_distinct": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_features": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_valence": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_color": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
}


@memo
def L0[u: UTT, r: OBJ](lex: ...):
    listener: knows(u)
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=at(lex, u, r))
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L1[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., prior: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r)
            * exp(alpha * log(L0[u, r](lex) + {EPS})),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L2[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., prior: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r)
            * exp(alpha * log(L1[u, r](alpha, lex, prior) + {EPS})),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


def listener(params, ctx):
    diffs = jnp.abs(ctx.lex[:, :, None] - ctx.lex[:, None, :])
    pair_dist = jnp.sum(diffs * (1.0 - ctx.is_sink[:, None, None]), axis=0)
    gray_diff = jnp.abs(ctx.grayscale[:, None] - ctx.grayscale[None, :])
    fam_diff = jnp.abs(
        ctx.familiarization[:, None] - ctx.familiarization[None, :]
    )
    total_dist = pair_dist + gray_diff + fam_diff
    duplicate_count = jnp.sum(total_dist == 0, axis=1)
    is_singleton = jnp.where(duplicate_count == 1, 1.0, 0.0)

    real_lex = ctx.lex * (1.0 - ctx.is_sink[:, None])
    diff = jnp.abs(real_lex[:, :, None] - real_lex[:, None, :])
    distinct = jnp.sum(diff, axis=(0, 2))

    effective_w_features = (
        params["w_features"] + ctx.valence * params["w_valence"]
    )

    prior = softmax_prior(
        params["w_singleton"] * is_singleton
        + params["w_distinct"] * distinct
        + effective_w_features * ctx.feature_count
        + params["w_color"] * (1.0 - ctx.grayscale)
    )

    heard = L2(params["alpha"], ctx.lex, prior)[ctx.utterance]
    return jnp.where(ctx.is_prior > 0, prior, heard)

"""Helpers every memo model file may import.

memo parses its own language: an array parameter (declared ``lex: ...``) can
only be read through a function call, never subscripted (``lex[u, r]`` parses
as a query about an agent). These JIT-compiled indexers are that call.

``OBJ`` and ``UTT`` are not here: the loader injects them, sized to the
context shape being evaluated (`src.rsa.model_file`).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

# Added inside log() so a zero probability gives a large finite penalty, not
# -inf and a NaN gradient.
EPS = 1e-10


@jax.jit
def at(matrix, i, j):
    """matrix[i, j] for an array parameter (e.g. the lexicon at [u, r])."""
    return matrix[i, j]


@jax.jit
def vec(vector, i):
    """vector[i] for an array parameter (e.g. a prior over objects at r)."""
    return vector[i]


def with_lapse(p: jnp.ndarray, lapse) -> jnp.ndarray:
    """Mix a choice distribution with a uniform guess over the objects.

    With probability ``lapse`` the participant picks an object at random.
    Without some such noise a model that gives an object probability zero
    (the literal semantics of RSA does, for any object the word is false of)
    makes one participant's choice of it an impossible event.
    """

4:     Speakers in reference games actively avoid referring expressions that are shared

6:     are penalized proportionally to their feature overlap with alternative referents

10: - name: isolated_graded_costly_l3
11:   rationale: Pragmatic listener at depth 3 with perceptual isolation, graded semantics,
12:     and utterance extension costs. Refines isolated_graded_costly_l2 by increasing
13:     the recursion depth from depth 2 to depth 3. Listeners reason at depth 3, inverting
14:     a speaker who simulates a depth-2 pragmatic listener. Visual pop-out is determined
15:     by an object's perceptual isolation (minimum Hamming distance to any other context
16:     object), semantic applicability diminishes with additional competing features
17:     (graded truth), and speakers evaluate communicative utility trade-offs with utterance
18:     extension costs proportional to the fraction of display objects sharing each feature.
19:     On uninformative prior trials, choice follows the perceptual isolation prior.
20:     A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.
21: - name: oddity_heuristic_listener
22:   rationale: Perceptual oddity heuristic listener. Listeners interpret referring expressions
23:     using a perceptual oddity heuristic rather than recursive Theory of Mind. When
24:     hearing a word that applies to multiple referents, listeners select the contextually
25:     unique singleton that lacks identical duplicates in the visual display. On uninformative
26:     trials without an informative word, listeners spontaneously choose the unique
27:     singleton, defaulting to uniform choice when all items are distinct or no oddity
28:     contrast exists. A lapse parameter captures random clicking.

30:   rationale: 'RSA pragmatic listener at depth 2 with singleton salience, contextual
31:     distinctiveness, visual feature complexity, evaluative valence framing, visual
32:     color contrast, and literal L0. Refining rsa_l2_singleton_distinct_feat_color_l0
33:     by incorporating the evaluative valence framing component from polarity_congruence_listener:
34:     speakers and listeners reason at depth 2 (inverting a speaker who simulates a
35:     depth-1 pragmatic listener) with common knowledge of an object prior combining
36:     discrete visual singleton salience (favoring unique objects with no duplicates
37:     in the scene), continuous contextual distinctiveness (favoring objects with greater
38:     feature contrast relative to the rest of the display), visual feature complexity
39:     modulated by evaluative framing valence (favoring feature-rich items under neutral/positive
40:     framing but inverting to favor sparse, featureless items when referring to a least
41:     favorite object), and visual color contrast (favoring fully colored objects over
42:     desaturated grayscale distractors). Crucially, the foundational simulated literal
43:     listener L0 operates purely on truth-conditional semantics without perceptual
44:     bias, preventing redundant prior compounding across reasoning tiers. On prior
45:     trials with no informative word, choices are governed directly by the combined

47: - name: rsa_l2

  rationale: Pragmatic listener reasoning about a competitor-confusion-averse speaker.
    Speakers in reference games actively avoid referring expressions that are shared
    with visually similar or confusable distractors in the context. Candidate words
    are penalized proportionally to their feature overlap with alternative referents
    that also satisfy the word. Pragmatic listeners invert this confusion-averse speaker,
    expecting words to target referents whose competitors are visually distinct rather
    than near-identical clones.
- name: isolated_graded_costly_l3
  rationale: Pragmatic listener at depth 3 with perceptual isolation, graded semantics,
    and utterance extension costs. Refines isolated_graded_costly_l2 by increasing
    the recursion depth from depth 2 to depth 3. Listeners reason at depth 3, inverting
    a speaker who simulates a depth-2 pragmatic listener. Visual pop-out is determined
    by an object's perceptual isolation (minimum Hamming distance to any other context
    object), semantic applicability diminishes with additional competing features
    (graded truth), and speakers evaluate communicative utility trade-offs with utterance
    extension costs proportional to the fraction of display objects sharing each feature.
    On uninformative prior trials, choice follows the perceptual isolation prior.
    A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.
- name: oddity_heuristic_listener
  rationale: Perceptual oddity heuristic listener. Listeners interpret referring expressions
    using a perceptual oddity heuristic rather than recursive Theory of Mind. When
    hearing a word that applies to multiple referents, listeners select the contextually
    unique singleton that lacks identical duplicates in the visual display. On uninformative
    trials without an informative word, listeners spontaneously choose the unique
    singleton, defaulting to uniform choice when all items are distinct or no oddity
    contrast exists. A lapse parameter captures random clicking.
- name: rsa_l2_singleton_feat_color_valence_l0
  rationale: 'RSA pragmatic listener at depth 2 with singleton salience, contextual
    distinctiveness, visual feature complexity, evaluative valence framing, visual
    color contrast, and literal L0. Refining rsa_l2_singleton_distinct_feat_color_l0
    by incorporating the evaluative valence framing component from polarity_congruence_listener:
    speakers and listeners reason at depth 2 (inverting a speaker who simulates a
    depth-1 pragmatic listener) with common knowledge of an object prior combining
    discrete visual singleton salience (favoring unique objects with no duplicates
    in the scene), continuous contextual distinctiveness (favoring objects with greater
    feature contrast relative to the rest of the display), visual feature complexity
    modulated by evaluative framing valence (favoring feature-rich items under neutral/positive
    framing but inverting to favor sparse, featureless items when referring to a least
    favorite object), and visual color contrast (favoring fully colored objects over
    desaturated grayscale distractors). Crucially, the foundational simulated literal
    listener L0 operates purely on truth-conditional semantics without perceptual
    bias, preventing redundant prior compounding across reasoning tiers. On prior
    trials with no informative word, choices are governed directly by the combined
    perceptual prior. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.'
- name: rsa_l2
  rationale: 'RSA pragmatic listener at depth 2, uniform prior over objects. One more
    level of recursion than the vanilla model: a speaker S2 chooses words by how well
    the depth-1 pragmatic listener L1 would recover the object (exp(alpha * log L1)),
    and the listener L2 inverts S2. Depth-2 reasoning is what the pragmods "complex"
    game needs to single out the object described by the twice-implicated word. One
    rationality alpha at every level; uniform choice with no informative word; a lapse
    parameter mixes in uniform guessing.'
- name: rsa_l1
  rationale: Vanilla RSA pragmatic listener (depth 1), uniform prior over objects.
    The listener reasons about a speaker who chooses a true word with probability
    proportional to exp(alpha * log L0(object | word)), where L0 is the literal listener;
    the listener inverts that speaker with a uniform prior over objects (Frank & Goodman,
    2012). With no informative word the choice is uniform. A lapse parameter mixes
    in uniform guessing.

# Ported from competitor_confusion_speaker.py by src.rsa_open.port, rule (a) (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §3.1).
"""Pragmatic listener reasoning about a competitor-confusion-averse speaker.

Speakers in reference games actively avoid referring expressions that are shared
with visually similar or confusable distractors in the context. Candidate words
are penalized proportionally to their feature overlap with alternative referents
that also satisfy the word. Pragmatic listeners invert this confusion-averse
speaker, expecting words to target referents whose competitors are visually
distinct rather than near-identical clones.
"""

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro.distributions as dist
from memo import memo

from src.rsa.memo_kit import EPS, at, softmax_prior, with_lapse

PARAMS = {
    "alpha": dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_confusion": dist.Normal(0.0, 2.0),
}


@memo
def L0[u: UTT, r: OBJ](lex: ...):
    listener: knows(u)
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=at(lex, u, r))
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L1[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, w_confusion, lex: ..., confusion: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=1),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r)
            * exp(
                alpha * log(L0[u, r](lex) + {EPS})
                - w_confusion * at(confusion, u, r)
            ),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


def compute_confusion_and_prior(ctx, w_confusion):
    feats = jnp.vstack([ctx.lex, ctx.grayscale[None, :], ctx.familiarization[None, :]])
    diff = feats[:, :, None] - feats[:, None, :]
    dist = jnp.sum(jnp.abs(diff), axis=0)
    n_obj = dist.shape[0]
    eye = jnp.eye(n_obj)
    sim = jnp.exp(-dist) * (1.0 - eye)

    real_words = (1.0 - ctx.is_sink)[:, None]
    real_lex = ctx.lex * real_words

    confusion = real_lex @ sim
    baseline_confusion = jnp.sum(sim, axis=1)
    prior = softmax_prior(-w_confusion * baseline_confusion)
    return confusion, prior


def listener(params, ctx):
    confusion, prior = compute_confusion_and_prior(ctx, params["w_confusion"])
    heard = L1(params["alpha"], params["w_confusion"], ctx.lex, confusion)[ctx.utterance]
    return jnp.where(ctx.is_prior > 0, prior, heard)

"""Pragmatic listener at depth 3 with perceptual isolation, graded semantics, and utterance extension costs.

Refines isolated_graded_costly_l2 by increasing the recursion depth from depth 2 to depth 3.
Listeners reason at depth 3, inverting a speaker who simulates a depth-2 pragmatic listener.
Visual pop-out is determined by an object's perceptual isolation (minimum Hamming distance to
any other context object), semantic applicability diminishes with additional competing features
(graded truth), and speakers evaluate communicative utility trade-offs with utterance extension
costs proportional to the fraction of display objects sharing each feature. On uninformative
prior trials, choice follows the perceptual isolation prior. A lapse parameter mixes in
uniform guessing.
"""

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro.distributions as dist
from memo import memo

from src.rsa.memo_kit import EPS, at, softmax_prior, vec, with_lapse

PARAMS = {
    "alpha": dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_distinct": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "gamma": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "cost_weight": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
}


def object_isolation(lex: jnp.ndarray, is_sink: jnp.ndarray) -> jnp.ndarray:
    """Minimum Hamming distance of each object to any other object in the display."""
    features = lex * (1.0 - is_sink)[:, None]
    diff = jnp.abs(features[:, :, None] - features[:, None, :])
    pair_dist = jnp.sum(diff, axis=0)
    n_obj = lex.shape[1]
    eye = jnp.eye(n_obj) * 1e5
    return jnp.min(pair_dist + eye, axis=1)


def compute_graded_lex(lex: jnp.ndarray, feature_count: jnp.ndarray, is_sink: jnp.ndarray, gamma) -> jnp.ndarray:
    """Compute graded truth values where applicability diminishes with additional features."""
    fc = jnp.maximum(feature_count, 1.0)
    precision = jnp.exp(-gamma * (fc - 1.0))
    real_truth = lex * precision[None, :]
    return jnp.where(is_sink[:, None] > 0, lex, real_truth)


@memo
def L0[u: UTT, r: OBJ](lex: ...):
    listener: knows(u)
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=at(lex, u, r))
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L1[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., prior: ..., cost: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r) * exp(alpha * (log(L0[u, r](lex) + {EPS}) - vec(cost, u))),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L2[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., prior: ..., cost: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r) * exp(alpha * (log(L1[u, r](alpha, lex, prior, cost) + {EPS}) - vec(cost, u))),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L3[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., prior: ..., cost: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r) * exp(alpha * (log(L2[u, r](alpha, lex, prior, cost) + {EPS}) - vec(cost, u))),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


def listener(params, ctx):
    graded_lex = compute_graded_lex(ctx.lex, ctx.feature_count, ctx.is_sink, params["gamma"])
    dist_vec = object_isolation(ctx.lex, ctx.is_sink)
    prior = softmax_prior(params["w_distinct"] * dist_vec)
    ext = jnp.sum(ctx.lex, axis=-1) / ctx.lex.shape[-1]
    cost = params["cost_weight"] * ext
    heard = L3(params["alpha"], graded_lex, prior, cost)[ctx.utterance]
    return jnp.where(ctx.is_prior > 0, prior, heard)

exp1_block = next(b for b in blocks if b.name == 'exp1')
theory = TheoryModel(Path('_runs/chain_0/experiment1/loop/models/rsa_l2_singleton_feat_color_valence_l0.py'))

params = {
    'alpha': jnp.array(0.903),
    'w_singleton': jnp.array(1.389),
    'w_distinct': jnp.array(0.099),
    'w_features': jnp.array(0.025),
    'w_valence': jnp.array(0.974),
    'w_color': jnp.array(0.520),
}

c = exp1_block.contexts[37]

# Ported from oddity_heuristic_listener.py by src.rsa_open.port, rule (a) (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §3.1).
"""Perceptual oddity heuristic listener.

Listeners interpret referring expressions using a perceptual oddity heuristic
rather than recursive Theory of Mind. When hearing a word that applies to
multiple referents, listeners select the contextually unique singleton that
lacks identical duplicates in the visual display. On uninformative trials
without an informative word, listeners spontaneously choose the unique
singleton, defaulting to uniform choice when all items are distinct or no
oddity contrast exists. A lapse parameter captures random clicking.
"""

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro.distributions as dist
from memo import memo

from src.rsa.memo_kit import at, softmax_prior, vec, with_lapse

PARAMS = {
    "beta": dist.Normal(0.0, 2.0),
}


@memo
def L_heur[u: UTT, r: OBJ](beta, lex: ..., is_singleton: ...):
    listener: knows(u)
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=at(lex, u, r) * exp(beta * vec(is_singleton, r)))
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


def compute_singleton_indicator(ctx):
    feats = jnp.vstack([ctx.lex, ctx.grayscale[None, :], ctx.familiarization[None, :]])
    diff = feats[:, :, None] - feats[:, None, :]
    dist = jnp.sum(jnp.abs(diff), axis=0)
    is_identical = (dist < 1e-5).astype(jnp.float32)
    copy_count = jnp.sum(is_identical, axis=1)
    is_singleton = (copy_count <= 1.0).astype(jnp.float32)
    return is_singleton


def listener(params, ctx):
    is_singleton = compute_singleton_indicator(ctx)
    prior = softmax_prior(params["beta"] * is_singleton)
    heard = L_heur(params["beta"], ctx.lex, is_singleton)[ctx.utterance]
    return jnp.where(ctx.is_prior > 0, prior, heard)

display.text:
"""Self-check for a theorist's theory: the open loop's admission gates with a short fit.

    <the harness python> -m src.rsa_open.loop.check_candidate <candidate_dir> --corpus <corpus.json>

Runs the code gate, the theory checks, the listener and speaker contracts on the corpus and
the novelty pool, and a short fit to every paradigm at once. It does not run the novelty
comparison (that needs the loop's set) and reports non-convergence of the short fit as a
warning, since the loop's fit is longer. Exit code 0 when nothing fails.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import tyro

from src.rsa.fit import FitSettings
from src.rsa.loop.novelty import plain_pool
from src.rsa_open.loop.fitting import read_corpus
from src.rsa_open.loop.gates import GateConfig, admit

CHECK_SETTINGS = FitSettings(num_warmup=300, num_samples=300, num_chains=2, dense_mass=True)
CHECK_TIME_LIMIT_SEC = 15 * 60


@dataclass
class Args:
    candidate_dir: tyro.conf.Positional[Path]
    corpus: Path


def check(candidate_dir: Path, corpus: Path) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as cache:
        cfg = GateConfig(corpus, Path(cache), CHECK_SETTINGS, novelty_threshold=0.0,
                         time_limit_sec=CHECK_TIME_LIMIT_SEC)
        out = admit(candidate_dir, "candidate", cfg=cfg, blocks=read_corpus(corpus), pool=plain_pool(),
                    admitted_preds={})
    if out.admitted:
        return True, ("PASS: the theory meets every gate the self-check runs. The loop also checks novelty "
                      "against the theories in the set.")
    if out.reason.startswith("the fit did not converge"):
        return True, ("WARNING (not a failure of the self-check): the short fit did not converge "
                      f"({out.reason}). The loop fits longer; if your theory has parameters the data cannot "
                      "pin down, reparameterise.")
    return False, f"FAIL: {out.reason}"


def main(args: Args) -> int:
    ok, message = check(args.candidate_dir, args.corpus)
    print(message)
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from src.rsa.cpus import pin_main_thread

    'w_features': jnp.array(0.025),
    'w_valence': jnp.array(0.974),
    'w_color': jnp.array(0.520),
}

    l = np.asarray(class_probs(incumbent.group_probs(params, group)[None], group.classes)[0])
    s = np.asarray(incumbent.group_speaker(params, group))
    parts_inc += [l.reshape(-1), s.reshape(-1)]
preds_inc = np.concatenate(parts_inc)

        gray_diff = jnp.abs(ctx.grayscale[:, None] - ctx.grayscale[None, :])

        total_dist = pair_dist + gray_diff + fam_diff

        num_singletons = jnp.sum(duplicate_count == 1)
        is_singleton = jnp.where((duplicate_count == 1) & (num_singletons == 1), 1.0, 0.0)

        real_lex = ctx.lex * (1.0 - ctx.is_sink[:, None])
        diff = jnp.abs(real_lex[:, :, None] - real_lex[:, None, :])
        distinct = jnp.sum(diff, axis=(0, 2))

        effective_w_features = p['w_features'] + ctx.valence * p['w_valence']

        prior = softmax_prior(
            p['w_singleton'] * is_singleton
            + p['w_distinct'] * distinct
            + effective_w_features * ctx.feature_count
            + p['w_color'] * (1.0 - ctx.grayscale)
        )
        heard = mod.L2(p['alpha'], ctx.lex, prior)[ctx.utterance]
        return jnp.where(ctx.is_prior > 0, prior, heard)

    vmapped_l = jax.vmap(lambda a: cand_listener(params, a))(group.arrays)

        real_words = (1.0 - ctx.is_sink)[:, None]
        s_unnorm = all_l * real_words
        return s_unnorm / jnp.maximum(s_unnorm.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True), 1e-10)
    vmapped_s = jax.vmap(lambda a: cand_speaker(params, a))(group.arrays)

    s = np.asarray(vmapped_s)
    parts_cand += [l.reshape(-1), s.reshape(-1)]
